name: NMI due to watchdog
meaning: The watchdog on the closed-loop control module expired, which points to a hardware fault in the module's time base.
symptoms: Drive faults at power-up or at random and will not stay ready.
causes: Failed control module hardware; poorly seated module or memory module; electrical noise.
checks: Power off, reseat the control module and memory module, check grounding and shielding, then power on. If it returns, the control module has failed.
repairable: Yes: 611U control modules are repaired at component level and tested on a drive.
service: Servo drive repair; controller card & PCB repair

name: Checksum test error
meaning: The checksum test of the program or data memory failed, so the firmware or its memory is corrupt.
symptoms: Fault at power-up; the axis never becomes ready.
causes: Memory fault on the control module; corrupted firmware.
checks: Power cycle once. If it repeats, reload firmware with a known-good memory module; if it still repeats, the control module needs repair.
repairable: Yes: 611U control modules are repaired at component level and tested on a drive.
service: Servo drive repair; controller card & PCB repair

name: NMI due to cycle failure
meaning: The control module's basic cycle failed, either from electrical noise or a hardware fault.
symptoms: Random trips, sometimes when nearby equipment switches.
causes: Poor grounding or shielding; loose plug-in connections; control module hardware fault.
checks: Check plug-in connections, cabinet grounding and noise suppression on contactors and brakes. If it continues on a clean installation, the module is faulty.
repairable: Yes: 611U control modules are repaired at component level and tested on a drive.
service: Servo drive repair; controller card & PCB repair

name: Actual current sensing during power-up
meaning: At power-up the drive expected zero current but measured current, so the current-sensing hardware is suspect.
symptoms: Fault every time the drive powers up, before the motor turns.
causes: Faulty current sensors or measuring circuit in the power section; poorly seated control module; control module fault.
checks: With power off, reseat the control module in the power section and check its connectors. If the fault stays, the power section or control module needs repair.
repairable: Yes: current-sensing faults in the power section and control module are repairable.

Measuring circuit error, motor measuring system
meaning: The signal from the motor encoder is too weak or faulty, or the cable-break monitor tripped.
symptoms: Fault on enable or while running, often when the cable moves or the machine vibrates.
causes: Damaged or wrong encoder cable; poor shield connection; loose connector; failed encoder; faulty encoder input on the control module.
checks: Check the encoder cable along its length and at both connectors; make sure the shield is clamped; swap in a known-good cable if you have one.
repairable: Yes: encoders, encoder cables and the drive's encoder input are all repairable.
service: Encoder repair; servo motor repair; custom cables

name: Measuring circuit error, motor measuring system absolute track
meaning: The absolute track of the motor encoder is interrupted, or an EnDat absolute encoder failed to initialize.
symptoms: Fault at power-up or after a cable is disturbed; position is lost.
causes: Wrong cable type or damaged cable; encoder type set wrong in the drive; failed absolute encoder.
checks: Confirm the cable is the correct type for the encoder; check the encoder type parameter; inspect the connectors for bent pins.
repairable: Yes: absolute encoders are repaired or replaced and aligned to the motor.

name: Synchronization error, rotor position
meaning: The rotor position from the encoder disagrees with the fine-synchronized position by more than 45 electrical degrees.
symptoms: Fault on enable; the motor may jerk, run rough or lack torque.
causes: Encoder slipped on the shaft or replaced without alignment; noisy encoder signals from poor grounding or shielding; failed encoder.
checks: Check encoder cabling, grounding and shield; ask whether the motor or encoder was recently changed (it may need re-alignment).
repairable: Yes: we re-align encoders to the motor and test under drive control.

name: Zero mark monitoring, motor measuring system
meaning: The measured rotor position changes between two zero marks, which means encoder pulses are being lost.
symptoms: Fault while running, often at higher speed or when the cable flexes.
causes: Intermittent encoder cable or connector; poor shielding; dirty or failing encoder.
checks: Check the cable and connectors, especially in cable tracks; make sure the shield is clamped at the drive.

Power module temperature exceeded
meaning: The power module heatsink is too hot. The drive warns first and shuts down about 20 seconds later.
symptoms: Trips after running a while under load, or in a hot cabinet.
causes: Failed or clogged module fan; blocked airflow; high cabinet temperature; too much load for the module size.
checks: Check the fan and airflow through the module; clean dust; measure the cabinet temperature.
repairable: Yes: fans are replaced and power modules repaired and tested.
service: Servo drive repair; cooling fan replacement

Error in AD conversion, terminal 56/14 or 24/20
meaning: The control module made a timing error while reading its analog-to-digital converter, so analog values may be wrong.
symptoms: Fault on power-up or during operation; analog setpoints may misbehave.
causes: Hardware fault on the closed-loop control module.
checks: Power cycle once. If it returns, the control module needs repair.
repairable: Yes: 611U control modules are repaired at component level and tested on a drive.
service: Servo drive repair; controller card & PCB repair

Current controller output limited
meaning: The current controller hit its output limit: the drive cannot push the requested current into the motor.
symptoms: Fault on enable or under load; the motor may not move.
causes: Motor disconnected or a phase missing (cable, contactor); DC link voltage missing; failed power section.
checks: With power off, check the motor cable and any motor contactor; measure winding resistance phase to phase; check the DC link supply.
repairable: Yes: power sections and motors are both repairable.
service: Servo drive repair; servo motor repair

name: Speed controller output limited
meaning: The speed controller stayed at its limit for too long: the motor cannot reach the requested speed.
symptoms: Fault on enable or when the axis starts moving; the axis may run away or not move.
causes: Motor brake not releasing; mechanical blocking; wrong motor or encoder wiring; encoder fault; incorrect controller data.
checks: Check that the brake releases; turn the axis by hand to feel for blocking; check motor phase order and encoder cable.
repairable: Yes: brakes, encoders and motors are repaired and tested under drive control.
service: Servo motor repair; encoder repair; motor brake repair

Illegal current during rotor position identification
Shutdown limit, motor overtemperature exceeded
meaning: The motor's temperature sensor reading went above the shutdown limit.
symptoms: Trips after the axis has worked hard; trips at once if the sensor circuit is faulty.
causes: Motor overloaded or cycled too hard; failed motor fan; faulty temperature sensor; break in the sensor wires in the encoder cable.
checks: Feel whether the motor is really hot; check the motor fan; check the sensor wiring in the encoder cable.
repairable: Yes: sensor replacement, bearing work and rewinding are routine motor repairs.

name: DC link undervoltage
meaning: The DC link voltage fell below the lower limit.
symptoms: Trips when the line supply dips or the infeed drops out.
causes: Line supply problem; infeed or supply module fault; braking resistor overloaded.
checks: Check the line supply and the infeed module status; check the braking resistor.
repairable: Yes: infeed and supply modules are repaired at component level.
service: Servo drive repair; line module repair

name: DC link overvoltage
meaning: The DC link voltage rose above the upper limit, usually from braking energy.
causes: Braking energy too high for the regen or braking resistor; high line voltage; failed pulse resistor or infeed module.
checks: Check the line voltage; reduce the deceleration as a test; check the pulsed resistor module or regenerative infeed.
repairable: Yes: infeed and resistor modules are repairable.
service: Servo drive repair; line module repair
